title: status.json — whose turn it is, and what has already repeated (4.4 rule 4, 6.2)
description: Not a card: a thread ledger. It carries no numbers, so it needs no grades. It says who owes the next move, what pair of (reason_code, parameter) has already come back twice, and which round trips were replaced by a knowledge reference instead of reopened. Four sessions and no such line is four windows nobody can follow (6.2).

round.description: the highest round on disk for this thread. A thread with no round is not a thread.

turn.description: never the bridge: it moves cards, so it never owes a move. Never the librarian either: the librarian answers, it does not take turns.

state.description: open means an agent owes the next card. held means a gate could not be resolved and a person has to resolve it (4.4 failure table). escalated means a (reason_code, parameter) pair came back twice and no further round may open (4.4 rule 6). closed means the thread is done.

blocked_pairs.description: The repetition ledger. There is no fixed round cap: a number cuts off round trips that are making progress, and ones going in circles are already waste before they reach it (4.4 rule 6).

rounds.description: the rounds this pair was refused in. Two entries call the human.

substitutions.description: A round that was not opened because the same observable and conditions had already crossed, and a knowledge entry answers it (4.4 rule 5). Needs the librarian: with no knowledge store to point at there is nothing to substitute, which is why a degraded bridge reopens the round instead.

open_question.description: required when state is held: what a person has to answer, and where it is recorded (e.g. plan.md 11-1)
